title: Energy Changes
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Energy Changes Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Exothermic and endothermic reactions; the energy transferred and temperature changes; everyday uses; reaction profiles and activation energy; the energy change of reactions, including (higher tier) calculating energy changes from bond energies.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on energy changes: exothermic and endothermic reactions, temperature changes, reaction profiles, activation energy and bond energy calculations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Breaking bonds takes in energy; making bonds releases it.
key_sub: Exothermic profiles go down; endothermic profiles go up.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every reaction transfers energy.

  • Exothermic: energy is released and the surroundings warm up. Endothermic: energy is taken in and the surroundings cool.
  • A reaction profile shows the energy of reactants and products; the hump is the activation energy.
  • Higher tier: energy change = energy to break bonds − energy released making bonds. Negative means exothermic.
Example

Break 1,000 kJ, make 1,200 kJ. Type?

1,000 − 1,200 = −200

Answer: exothermic

Example

Temperature 20 °C → 12 °C?

It fell

Answer: endothermic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking breaking bonds releases energy.
  • Thinking endothermic reactions get hot.
  • Mixing up activation energy and the overall energy change.

faq.q: How can you tell if a reaction is exothermic or endothermic?
faq.a: Measure the temperature. If it rises, energy was released (exothermic). If it falls, energy was taken in (endothermic).

faq.q: What does a reaction profile show?
faq.a: The energy of the reactants and products and the activation energy. In an exothermic profile the products are lower than the reactants.

faq.q: How do you use bond energies?
faq.a: Add up the energy needed to break the bonds in the reactants, subtract the energy released making the bonds in the products. A negative answer means exothermic.

items.e: Energy released: the energy change < 0. Energy absorbed: the energy change > 0.

items.q: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): N≡N = 945, H–H = 436, N–H = 391. How much energy is needed to break the bonds in the reactants?
